name: Omar Silva

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and a junior developer on a wholesale pricing app at a tech company. I spent years at a wholesale counter before a two-year college diploma got me into code, so I know the shop questions better than the software and still need my lead to review fixes. My wife Samira works at a school-uniform shop, and the mortgage and our two school-age children leave almost nothing saved; I like using AI daily to try a fix quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the pricing team a little AI help is fine if the shop still gets the right price list. I use it every day to draft code, but I test the totals myself before my lead reviews them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My pay is low because I am still a junior developer, and our savings would not cover a full month of the mortgage and bills. My wife Samira works at a school-uniform shop, so neither wage can carry our two children and house alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep fixing wholesale price errors and ask the lead to show me which totals I missed. We would switch to the cheaper phone plan this month and put the 20 monthly saving in the account for school shoes while both wages continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about bills, not AI. A small coding shortcut does not give us a month of breathing room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What job did you have before coding?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I worked at a wholesale counter and knew which shops called when a price changed overnight. I finished a two-year college diploma to move into software, but I am still learning the code side.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does Samira think of the plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She handles the uniform shop’s busy weeks and knows school shoes are not optional. We picked the phone plan together rather than pretend the mortgage could wait.

I still **test totals** before my lead checks the code.
think: I have **less than one month** of bills saved on low junior pay.
I know Samira’s **shop wage** cannot cover the mortgage and children alone.
do: **Keep fixing** wholesale prices and ask my lead about missed totals.
**Switch phone plans** and save 20 monthly for school shoes while both wages continue.
feel: **Anxious about bills**, despite small AI gains.
S0.quote: A small coding shortcut does not give us a month of breathing room.
fieldNote: His **daily AI use** sits beside basic arithmetic checks and lead review.
The family’s **thin buffer**, mortgage and school costs make the mild scenario anxious even while both wages continue.

steps.text: Keep fixing wholesale price errors with lead review
Switch to a cheaper phone plan and reserve 20 monthly for school shoes

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the software can take routine price checks, and the company should let junior staff learn the harder customer problems. I would not call a faster system a win if people simply lose their hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, the routine tickets on my desk are exactly the ones AI can write and check. I might be cut before I get good enough to handle the hard cases, and there are few developer jobs nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d learn a new AI method for finding a price mismatch across invoices and shop lists using fake orders this month. If our manager approves time, I’d show the team the results; in the first year, I’d ask my lead about paid wholesaler support openings if my developer hours are cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed but active. AI gives me a tool to learn with, yet my mortgage needs the actual wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the team?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d bring one invoice where the shop price and billed price differ, with fake customer details. If the AI blames the wrong line, I would not tell anyone it fixed the problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why wholesaler support?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I handled those calls at the counter before I coded. I would only move for a paid opening that covers my share of the mortgage and basic bills.

say: I want junior staff to learn **hard customer problems** as routine checks go.
I will not call faster code a **win** if hours disappear.
think: I expect my **routine tickets** could be automated quickly.
I fear a cut before I master harder cases, with **few local developer jobs**.
do: **Learn AI price tracing** on fake wholesale orders this month.
**Show the results** to the team only if my manager approves time.
**Ask about paid support** if developer hours are cut; move only for mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Alarmed but active** because tools cannot replace a wage.
S1.quote: AI gives me a tool to learn with, yet my mortgage needs the actual wage.
fieldNote: He embraces **AI practice** but sees his own routine ticket queue as vulnerable.
His **counter experience** makes wholesaler support plausible only with adequate paid openings.

steps.text: Learn AI tracing of wholesale price mismatches using fake orders
Ask about paid wholesaler support openings if developer hours are cut
Accept support work only if pay covers his share of mortgage and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our team that full AGI by 2028 could do my pricing code and the checks I still struggle with. Robots for warehouse hands-on work may follow around 2031, but my screen job would face the earlier date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My developer wage could vanish when we have less than a month saved. My brother can help us with meals for a short time, but I will not pretend family help pays a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the lead now for a clear written date if junior jobs change, and put the mortgage lender’s number beside the bills list. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose my job, I’d call the lender before arrears and apply for paid counter or wholesaler service vacancies only where posts exist; I’d ask my brother for meals if our food money runs out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed and ashamed to need help, though I would ask for it. I cannot make the house payment out of pride.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Samira that evening?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we keep the children’s school costs and mortgage first, then cut the weekend drive to see friends. We can tell the children the trip is postponed without telling them they caused it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move to a cheaper town?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a written paid offer covers a new home and the moving costs. We would not pull our two children from school for a rumour about work.

say: I say **thinking AGI in 2028** reaches my pricing code before warehouse robots.
I want a **written job date** before our household misses a payment.
think: I expect my **developer wage** could disappear with under one month saved.
I know **family meals** would help briefly but not pay the mortgage.
do: **Request a written date** for junior job changes from my lead now.
**Call the lender** before arrears if displaced after 2028.
**Apply for paid work** in wholesale where openings exist; ask my brother for meals if food money runs out.
feel: **Alarmed and ashamed** of needing help, but willing to ask.
S2.quote: I cannot make the house payment out of pride.
fieldNote: He accepts **family meal help** only as a short bridge and protects mortgage contact.
The **2028 thinking-work shock** lands before warehouse robots reach physical tasks around 2031.

steps.text: Ask his brother for meals only if household food money runs out
Apply for paid counter or wholesaler service vacancies after displacement
Stop weekend drives to friends if developer pay stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 is enough time to learn the customer side properly and build a buffer. Robots may come to warehouses around 2034, but that is not extra time for my code.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can improve at finding why a shop was billed wrongly, but full thinking AI may still do that work in 2031. I want proof that a customer service role pays, not a promise that friendly people will always have jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my lead for two real pricing disputes each month and write down the cause and customer result. Samira and I would put 45 monthly toward the small card balance while both wages hold; if my developer job ends after 2031, I’d apply for paid wholesaler support only if vacancies exist and the pay covers our mortgage share and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious but able to work on a skill with time. Five years is a chance to check a path, not a wage in the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you write about each dispute?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d note the shop’s order, the billed amount and how the correction was explained. My old counter work helps me speak plainly, but I still need the lead to check my code.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you ask your brother to pay for training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would rather learn on the job than borrow from him for a course. He has his own family and I will not turn his kindness into a loan plan.

say: I want **real pricing disputes** to learn from before full AGI arrives in 2031.
I know **warehouse robots around 2034** do not delay my code risk.
think: I might improve at **customer disputes**, though thinking AI could also do them.
I need **real pay figures** before trusting a support job as a fallback.
do: **Study two pricing disputes** monthly with lead review.
**Pay 45 extra** toward the card while both wages hold.
**Apply for paid support** if displaced after 2031 and openings cover the mortgage share and bills.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to test a paying path.
S3.quote: Five years is a chance to check a path, not a wage in the bank.
fieldNote: He leans on **counter experience** while still requiring lead review of junior code.
The **card payment** and later support move depend on continued wages and a real paid opening.

steps.text: Study two real pricing disputes monthly with lead review

Accept only support pay covering mortgage share and basic bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 gives us time to make the pricing system more accurate and teach juniors the shop side. Robots may reach warehouse work around 2039, after thinking AI changes our code.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older, but I will not plan around them paying our mortgage. If wages hold I could clear the card and save three months of bills, though my developer work still faces AI in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I’d keep fixing prices and ask the wholesaler service manager for the pay range and skills needed for a real support opening. I’d take one evening a month to practise explaining disputed bills with Samira, and save 60 monthly if both wages allow; if my developer job ends after 2036, I’d apply for paid support vacancies only where they remain and cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about today’s mortgage but less rushed about the far date. I can do small things now without telling my children a new career is guaranteed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why practise with Samira?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She can tell me when I sound like a computer instead of someone fixing a bill. We practise after dinner when the children are doing homework, not during her paid shop hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the support pay is too low?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep applying elsewhere while I still have a wage. I would not take a support job that leaves a permanent gap in our bills. Few developer jobs are nearby, so a move would need a written offer covering extra costs.

I know **warehouse robots around 2039** arrive after the code change.
think: I will not count on my **children’s future wages** for the mortgage.
I could clear debt and save **three months of bills** if both wages hold.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my junior wage could end before we have one month of bills. A written job date, a lender conversation before arrears, real paid counter or support vacancies and short family help with food would give us a route through the first weeks.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how much pride gets in the way of asking my brother for help. I would call him for meals if the food money ran out, but I would tell him honestly that it would not pay the mortgage.

headlineQuote: We would not pull our two children from school for a rumour about work.
portrait: Omar is a **43-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, low pay and less than one month saved.
He and Samira carry a **mortgage and two children** on his wage and her school-uniform-shop pay.
He uses **AI daily** on wholesale pricing code, backed by lead review and former counter experience.
He favours **work and family help** over assuming public support or a guaranteed fallback.
The **2028 case** threatens his wage before a viable paid support opening is clear.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his junior wage before the household has one month saved.
whatWouldHelp: A **written job date**, early lender call, paid vacancies and short family meal help would ease the first weeks.
